F01.title: Kayaba Coffee
F01.intro: A cafe in an old wooden house, good for breakfast while enjoying the neighborhood atmosphere.
F01.route: Walk around Nippori and Yanaka → Ueno
F01.toConfirm: This small, popular cafe may have a wait. Check its current Monday closing schedule before visiting.

F02.title: CIBI Tokyo Store
F02.intro: A cafe and lifestyle store for a Western-style breakfast between Japanese meals.
F02.toConfirm: This card is for the Sendagi store. Check that you have not selected another CIBI location.

F03.title: Marutoyo
F03.intro: An onigiri shop for a quick breakfast while exploring the Tsukiji market area.
F03.toConfirm: Mainly for takeaway. Check Sundays, public holidays, and market closure days before visiting.

F04.title: Tonkatsu Yamabe Ueno
F04.intro: A casual tonkatsu meal option that fits well with sightseeing in Ueno.
F04.recommendedMenu: Pork loin cutlet set, pork fillet cutlet set
F04.route: Tokyo National Museum → Ueno and Ameyoko
F04.toConfirm: There may be a wait. Whether four people can sit together depends on availability at the time.

F05.title: Nemuro Hanamaru KITTE Marunouchi
F05.intro: A Hokkaido-style sushi restaurant where everyone can choose from different kinds of sushi.
F05.route: Tokyo Station → KITTE → Liquors Hasegawa → Ginza
F05.toConfirm: The listing says reservations are unavailable and guests take a queue number on site. Four-person booths may be available, with a possible wait. Do not confuse it with the closed Ginza branch.

F06.title: Ginza Kagari Main Store
F06.intro: A candidate for rich, creamy chicken-broth ramen.
F06.route: A meal during a Ginza shopping visit
F06.toConfirm: Allow for a possible wait; choose a day without a tightly scheduled reservation afterward.

F07.title: Asakusa Mugitoro Main Store
F07.intro: A restaurant for trying traditional Japanese dishes beyond sushi and meat.
F07.recommendedMenu: Barley rice with grated yam, tororo dishes
F07.toConfirm: The sticky texture of grated yam may not suit everyone. The first-floor lunch buffet is listed for weekdays only; check it separately from other floors and courses.

F08.title: Hantei Nezu Main Store
F08.intro: A family dinner option for skewered fried shrimp, vegetables, and meat in an atmospheric old building.
F08.toConfirm: Reservations are recommended. Check the current notice about regular Monday closures.

F09.title: Asakusa Imahan Kokusai-dori Main Store
F09.intro: A meat-focused option for a special family meal during the trip.
F09.toConfirm: Plan for a larger meal budget. Check the branch name so it is not confused with similarly named Imahan restaurants.

F10.title: Monja Kura
F10.intro: A restaurant where the family can share food cooked on a griddle.
F10.toConfirm: Check whether everyone likes monjayaki's soft texture. Confirm weekend waits and reservation options before visiting.

F11.title: Gonpachi Odaiba
F11.intro: A restaurant with a broad menu for dinner after sightseeing in Odaiba.
F11.recommendedMenu: Soba, grilled skewers, Japanese pub dishes
F11.route: Odaiba Marine Park → Aqua City → dinner
F11.toConfirm: Reservations are recommended. Ask separately about seats with a view. This is a different branch from Nishi-Azabu.

F12.title: Dandelion Chocolate Factory & Cafe Kuramae
F12.intro: A chocolate cafe for a warm break during winter sightseeing.
F12.toConfirm: Allow extra travel time from central Asakusa.

F13.title: Nakamura Tokichi Ginza
F13.intro: A cafe for Japanese tea and desserts during a shopping break.
F13.toConfirm: When busy, the cafe may stop taking names before the posted closing time.

F14.title: Shiseido Parlour Ginza Main Store Salon de Cafe
F14.intro: A candidate for elaborate desserts at a long-established Ginza cafe.
F14.toConfirm: Budget more than for a typical cafe. If also visiting Nakamura Tokichi that day, consider choosing one of the two.

F15.title: Suzukien Asakusa Main Store
F15.intro: A snack stop for anyone who enjoys a strong matcha flavor.
F15.toConfirm: In winter, plan this as a quick snack stop rather than a cafe for a long seated break.

V01.title: Senso-ji Temple
V01.intro: A well-known Tokyo temple to explore together with Kaminarimon Gate and Nakamise Shopping Street.
V01.route: Combine with an Asakusa meal, Kappabashi, or Tokyo Skytree

V02.title: Nezu Shrine
V02.intro: A peaceful place to walk past red torii gates and around the shrine grounds.
V02.route: Combine with Yanaka, Sendagi, and Hantei
V02.toConfirm: This is a December trip, so do not expect the spring azalea scenery.

V03.title: Tokyo National Museum
V03.intro: A museum for exploring Japanese art, crafts, and history.
V03.route: Combine with Ueno Park and Tonkatsu Yamabe
V03.toConfirm: Mondays are normally closed. Some galleries are listed as closed during the December 2026 trip; the open area is more limited from December 22 to 25. Check the official notice before visiting.

V04.title: Hamarikyu Gardens
V04.intro: A quiet walk through a Japanese garden with skyscrapers in the background.

V05.title: Odaiba Marine Park
V05.intro: A place to take family photos with views of Tokyo Bay and Rainbow Bridge.
V05.toConfirm: Plan an indoor break as well in case of cold winter winds.

S01.title: Ginza Mitsukoshi
S01.intro: A department store for shopping and browsing Japanese sweets, desserts, and food gifts in the basement food hall.
S01.route: Combine with Ginza restaurants and cafes

S02.title: GINZA SIX
S02.intro: A shopping complex for fashion and design, with the Ginza Tsutaya Books store on the sixth floor.
S02.route: Shopping → sixth-floor Tsutaya Books → fourth-floor Nakamura Tokichi
S02.toConfirm: Tsutaya Books is an attraction inside this venue, not a separate duplicate place card.

S03.title: Kappabashi Kitchenware Street
S03.intro: A street for browsing Japanese tableware, chopsticks, kitchen tools, and realistic food models.
S03.toConfirm: Opening days and hours vary by individual shop.

S04.title: Liquors Hasegawa Main Store
S04.intro: A candidate for comparing and buying whisky and other spirits.
S04.route: Tokyo Station and KITTE → Yaesu Underground Mall
S04.toConfirm: This is a liquor shop, not a bar. Check stock and prices of rare bottles and whether tastings are offered.

S05.title: Yanaka Ginza Shopping Street
S05.intro: A shopping street for local snacks, small gifts, and a feel for old Tokyo.
S05.route: Nippori hotel → Yanaka → Sendagi and Nezu

E01.title: Tokyo Disneyland
E01.intro: A theme park that could connect memories of an earlier family trip with this one.
E01.toConfirm: The catalog lists the 2026 Christmas event as November 11–December 25. Decide on the visit date and tickets separately; nothing is booked automatically.

E02.title: teamLab Planets TOKYO
E02.intro: An interactive digital art exhibition for moving around together and taking photos.
E02.toConfirm: Consider booking a timed ticket. Some areas involve bare feet and water. Do not confuse this with teamLab exhibitions elsewhere.

E03.title: Tokyo Cruise Water Bus from Asakusa
E03.intro: A water bus ride where the journey itself offers views of the Sumida River and Tokyo Bay.
E03.toConfirm: The map points to the Asakusa boarding area. Check sailings, direct routes, and weather for the chosen day before confirming.

E04.title: Tokyo Skytree Observation Deck
E04.intro: An observation deck for taking in Tokyo's scale and night views.
E04.toConfirm: Choose a day based on the weather and visibility. Decide on tickets separately.

E05.title: Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse Christmas Market
E05.intro: A possible day trip for harbor night views and a Christmas market.
E05.route: Minato Mirai walk → Red Brick Warehouse
E05.toConfirm: The catalog lists the 2026 event as November 20–December 25. Weigh this trip against time available for Tokyo sightseeing.
E05.duration: Half a day to a full day, including nearby walks and travel
